scope: Only the R5 same-boot inactive-guard timing incompatibility and the active-written/committed-missing rollback gap. Read-only source/AST inspection and author50 evidence attribution. No test, prior counterexample, original validator, Native or device call was executed by this recheck.

same_boot_fix.finding: R6 no longer invokes adapter.main or adapter.guard from same_boot_resume. It first reads the genuine prior complete result by exact pin, binds original schema/status, final pin, source owner, expected input SHA and original reader/history/current-bound flags, and requires the four chain fields to match the full normal-stop expected. It then calls unchanged validate_inputs with the full expected object, original_modules, validate_current with the actual returned stop intent/result, and validate_chain. Original archives must equal the freshly revalidated ordered records; consumed-marker absence and snapshot byte stability remain checked. This avoids asking the old inactive-only service guard to succeed during ExecStartPre.
preserved_checks: validate_inputs still verifies exact startup/config/manifest pins, current boot and source owner, genuine single normal-stop intent/result and independent pre-stop history source bindings including the5ca alias gates.

validate_current still calls original load_business_checkpoint and _sealed_source, checks current owner/source unit/manifest/monotonic domain, unconsumed final and all original primary/SFace/optional/Native/recovery lower bounds.
validate_chain and the entire original5ca adapter bytes are unchanged; there is no new traversal, seed, restore or forged receipt.

camera_check still runs quiet before the history helper. quiet is AST-identical to R5 and admits only its ordered helper state with no prior/live service or hardware owners. This recheck does not close the separately tracked B01 review.
same_boot_fix.provenance_boundary: The prior complete_result_pin must really come from unchanged original main while both services were normally inactive. The new wrapper validates a pinned receipt and rechecks semantics; it does not authenticate a receipt against a malicious root or turn a fabricated flag into stop proof.

commit_gap_fix.finding: Before the first UI/startup publication R6 computes exact active_after_raw, O_EXCL/fsync-creates active-source.after.json and seals its SHA in intent. The final active ledger CAS and committed marker use those same bytes. rollback hashes sealed-after against intent, permits missing committed, requires a present committed to equal sealed-after, and accepts the live ledger only when it is exact prior or exact sealed-after. It can therefore restore the known published-after state even when committed was never reached, without trusting current ledger contents as a new after source.
commit_gap_fix.newer_ledger_rejection: A regular newer ledger whose bytes are neither sealed before nor sealed after fails NEWER_ACTIVE_LEDGER_CONFLICT before the first UI/startup reversal. A tampered after file fails its intent SHA. A conflicting committed file also fails before source reversal. Final ledger reversal uses sealed-after as its expected CAS bytes, not a freshly blessed live read.
commit_gap_fix.prior_limitation_disposition: The old active-written/committed-missing manual HOLD limit is resolved for new R6 transactions with complete sealed before/after artifacts and normal-stop/no-owner rollback preconditions. Transactions lacking those new artifacts still require explicit manual reconciliation; no backfill or Native receipt creation is authorized.
commit_gap_fix.atomicity_boundary: This remains the existing multi-file, known-byte transaction under an exclusive writer freeze. It does not claim a kernel-wide atomic transaction across UI/startup/ledger.
